\section[kṣame]{\kn{ಕ್ಷಮೆ} (kṣame) — pardon, forgiveness}

\label{lesson:KA-C97-pardon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for hello, then the Kannada for are you well.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕ್ಷಮೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷಮೆ}} (\emph{kṣame}) — \textquotedblleft{}pardon, forgiveness\textquotedblright{}. You know its verb from \textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷಮಿಸಿ}} (\emph{kṣamisi}), \textquotedblleft{}excuse me\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷಮೆ} \kn{ಇರಲಿ}} (\emph{kṣame irali}) — \textquotedblleft{}please forgive me\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The noun behind excuse me.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣame}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣame}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kṣame irali}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for hello, then the Kannada for are you well, then say \emph{kṣame} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕ್ಷಮೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Pardon, forgiveness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paricaya]{\kn{ಪರಿಚಯ} (paricaya) — an introduction, acquaintance}

\label{lesson:KA-C97-introduction}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for are you well, then the Kannada for pardon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಪರಿಚಯ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಪರಿಚಯ}} (\emph{paricaya}) — \textquotedblleft{}an introduction, acquaintance\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಿಮ್ಮ} \kn{ಪರಿಚಯ} \kn{ಸಂತೋಷ}} (\emph{nimma paricaya santōṣa}) — \textquotedblleft{}pleased to meet you\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}your acquaintance is a joy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A formal pleased to meet you.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricaya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricaya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nimma paricaya santōṣa}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for are you well, then the Kannada for pardon, then say \emph{paricaya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಪರಿಚಯ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An introduction, acquaintance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ābhāri]{\kn{ಆಭಾರಿ} (ābhāri) — grateful, obliged}

\label{lesson:KA-C97-grateful}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for pardon, then the Kannada for an introduction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆಭಾರಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಭಾರಿ}} (\emph{ābhāri}) — \textquotedblleft{}grateful, obliged\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನಾನು} \kn{ನಿಮಗೆ} \kn{ಆಭಾರಿ}} (\emph{nānu nimage ābhāri}) — \textquotedblleft{}I am grateful to you\textquotedblright{}, a deeper thanks than \textbf{\kn{ಧನ್ಯವಾದ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A thank-you with more weight.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ābhāri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ābhāri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nānu nimage ābhāri}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for pardon, then the Kannada for an introduction, then say \emph{ābhāri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಆಭಾರಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Grateful, obliged\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mareyabēḍi]{\kn{ಮರೆಯಬೇಡಿ} (mareyabēḍi) — please don't forget}

\label{lesson:KA-C97-dontforget}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for an introduction, then the Kannada for grateful.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಮರೆಯಬೇಡಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಮರೆಯಬೇಡಿ}} (\emph{mareyabēḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}please don't forget\textquotedblright{}, from \textbf{\kn{ಮರೆ}} (\emph{mare}), \textquotedblleft{}to forget\textquotedblright{}, with the polite \textbf{‑\kn{ಬೇಡಿ}} of \textbf{\kn{ಚಿಂತೆ} \kn{ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿ}}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A kind reminder at parting.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mareyabēḍi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mareyabēḍi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mareyabēḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for an introduction, then the Kannada for grateful, then say \emph{mareyabēḍi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಮರೆಯಬೇಡಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please don't forget\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[daye]{\kn{ದಯೆ} (daye) — kindness, compassion}

\label{lesson:KA-C97-kindness}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for grateful, then the Kannada for don't forget.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ದಯೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ದಯೆ}} (\emph{daye}) — \textquotedblleft{}kindness, compassion\textquotedblright{}. It is the \emph{daya} inside \textbf{\kn{ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು}}, \textquotedblleft{}please\textquotedblright{}, the word the book took apart early on.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The kindness hidden inside please.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{daye}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{daye}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{daye}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for grateful, then the Kannada for don't forget, then say \emph{daye} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ದಯೆ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Kindness, compassion\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Who you are — a first pass}

\label{lesson:KA-R97-first-pass-people-work}



\begin{quote}
Ask a friend not to forget, and name the kindness inside please.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item name a grandson, a granddaughter, a relative, the neighbours and an uncle
  \item ask someone's address and home town; name a birthday, a wedding and a language
  \item name a school, a college and an office; ask someone's job; say you know English
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Grandson, granddaughter? (\textbf{\kn{ಮೊಮ್ಮಗ}, \kn{ಮೊಮ್ಮಗಳು}}.) Relative? (\textbf{\kn{ಸಂಬಂಧಿಕ}}.) Neighbours? (\textbf{\kn{ನೆರೆಯವರು}}.) Uncle? (\textbf{\kn{ಮಾವ}}.) Address? (\textbf{\kn{ವಿಳಾಸ}}.) Birthday? (\textbf{\kn{ಹುಟ್ಟುಹಬ್ಬ}}.) Wedding? (\textbf{\kn{ಮದುವೆ}}.) Home town? (\textbf{\kn{ಊರು}}.) Language? (\textbf{\kn{ಭಾಷೆ}}.) School, college, office? (\textbf{\kn{ಶಾಲೆ}, \kn{ಕಾಲೇಜು}, \kn{ಕಚೇರಿ}}.) Job? (\textbf{\kn{ಉದ್ಯೋಗ}}.) English? (\textbf{\kn{ಇಂಗ್ಲಿಷ್}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{A day of small talk — a second pass}

\label{lesson:KA-R97-second-pass-body-table-greetings}



\begin{quote}
You meet a friend at lunchtime. Ask if they have eaten, and what's new.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item you feel dizzy; it is hot and sticky; are you at ease?; I got hurt; I feel like vomiting
  \item ask for a snack, a spoon, a glass of water and a plate; ask the price
  \item not possible; not like that; oh, I see; maybe; certainly
  \item long time!; hello on the phone; are you well?
  \item please forgive me; pleased to meet you; I am grateful to you
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Dizzy? (\textbf{\kn{ತಲೆಸುತ್ತು}}.) Sultry? (\textbf{\kn{ಸೆಕೆ}}.) At ease? (\textbf{\kn{ಆರಾಮ}}.) A wound? (\textbf{\kn{ಗಾಯ}}.) Vomiting? (\textbf{\kn{ವಾಂತಿ}}.) Snack, spoon, glass, plate? (\textbf{\kn{ತಿಂಡಿ}, \kn{ಚಮಚ}, \kn{ಲೋಟ}, \kn{ತಟ್ಟೆ}}.) Price? (\textbf{\kn{ಬೆಲೆ}}.) Not possible? (\textbf{\kn{ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ}}.) Not like that? (\textbf{\kn{ಹಾಗಲ್ಲ}}.) Oh, I see? (\textbf{\kn{ಓಹೋ}}.) Maybe? (\textbf{\kn{ಇರಬಹುದು}}.) Certainly? (\textbf{\kn{ಖಚಿತವಾಗಿ}}.) Have you eaten? (\textbf{\kn{ಊಟ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತಾ}?}) What's new? (\textbf{\kn{ಏನು} \kn{ಸಮಾಚಾರ}?}) Long time? (\textbf{\kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ದಿನ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತು}}.) Hello? (\textbf{\kn{ಹಲೋ}}.) Are you well? (\textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷೇಮವೇ}?}) Pardon? (\textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷಮೆ}}.) Introduction? (\textbf{\kn{ಪರಿಚಯ}}.) Grateful? (\textbf{\kn{ಆಭಾರಿ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
